title: Unique Triplets Summing to Zero
statement: You are given a list of integers nums, which may contain duplicate values. Find every distinct triplet of values [a, b, c] drawn from three different positions of nums such that a + b + c == 0. Two triplets are considered the same if they contain the same multiset of values, so each distinct value-combination must appear at most once in your answer. Return the triplets as a list of lists, where each inner triplet is sorted in ascending order and the overall list of triplets is sorted lexicographically (compare first elements, then second, then third). If no triplet sums to zero, return an empty list.
hints: A brute-force check of every triple is O(n^3). What ordering could let you turn the inner search into a linear sweep from both ends?
Sort the values first. Fix the smallest element at index i, then use two pointers converging from i+1 and the end to hunt for a pair summing to -arr[i].

After recording a valid triplet, move both pointers inward AND skip past any neighbors equal to the value you just used; likewise skip a fixed element equal to the previous fixed element. This pointer-level skipping — not a set — is what keeps duplicates like [-1,-1,0,1,1,2] from emitting the same triplet twice.
